extracted.intended_audience: AoPS users (students, forum and wiki contributors) who want to create mathematical diagrams with Asymptote
extracted.subtask_description: Introductory guidance for using the Asymptote vector-graphics language to produce mathematical diagrams on the AoPS Wiki and forums, including embedding code, basic commands, and format/LaTeX compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymptote purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Asymptote is a powerful vector graphics language designed for creating mathematical diagrams and figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page describes Asymptote as suitable for mathematical diagrams and figures and refers users to a Quick Start Video. This frames expectations: Asymptote is intended for precise, publication-quality math graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output formats
rubrics_metrics.description: It can output images in either eps or pdf format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use EPS or PDF output depending on downstream needs (paper, LaTeX inclusion, etc.). These are the supported export formats highlighted by the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Asymptote is compatible with the standard mathematics typesetting language, LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Asymptote integrates with LaTeX, use it when figures need consistent math typesetting; expect labels and equations to match document fonts and formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymptote is a full programming language
rubrics_metrics.description: It is also a complete programming language, and has cleaner syntax than its predecessor, MetaPost, which was a language used only for two-dimensional graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat Asymptote code as programmatic — you can write structured code, use variables, functions, macros and packages (see Macros and Packages, Reference, Advanced Asymptote). Prefer programmatic constructs for complex or repeatable figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding Asymptote on AoPS Wiki
rubrics_metrics.description: You can use Asymptote on the AoPSWiki right now, by enclosing the Asymptote code within <asy>...</asy> tags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place raw Asymptote code between <asy> and </asy> tags in a wiki page to render the figure. The page provides an inline example showing code and the resulting image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding Asymptote on AoPS forums
rubrics_metrics.description: On the AoPS forums you can use [asy]..[/asy] to include Asymptote code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use forum-specific tag syntax [asy]...[/asy] when posting on AoPS message boards; the page gives a small example demonstrating the forum tag usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic drawing commands and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Example commands shown: draw((0,0)--(3,7),red); dot((0,0)); label("Produced with Asymptote "+version.VERSION,point(S),2S);
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use draw(...) for segments/paths, dot(...) for points, and label(...) for text labels. The example demonstrates simple figure construction and placement/formatting of labels; study these as templates for common tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of version and built-in utilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The example uses version.VERSION and point(S) in a label call: label("Produced with Asymptote "+version.VERSION,point(S),2S);
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asymptote exposes built-in variables and utility functions (e.g., version). Use these for dynamic text or positioning in labels; consult the Reference and Useful functions sections for more utilities.
